subject: Future Tech
title: Making Fuel on Mars
description: A 60-second lesson on Making Fuel on Mars.

hook.text: A return trip from Mars needs fuel, but launching it from Earth would be absurdly expensive. Better to make it there.

buildup.text: Mars' atmosphere is 96% CO2. The Sabatier reaction combines CO2 with hydrogen to produce methane and water.

discovery.text: NASA's MOXIE experiment on Perseverance extracted oxygen from Martian CO2 in 2021, a small but historic first.

twist.text: Scaling MOXIE from lab demo to rocket fuel factory requires 200 times more output and years of reliable operation.

climax.text: SpaceX's Raptor engines burn methane and oxygen, the exact fuels ISRU can produce on Mars. The chemistry aligns.

punchline.text: The Martian atmosphere is a gas station waiting to open.

quiz.question: What did NASA's MOXIE experiment produce on Mars?
